Universal architecture: Sensor connects to SoC CSI receiver when electrical lanes, data type, clock, bit depth and ISP/PWL support match.
Compatible compute families: TI Jacinto/AM6x, NVIDIA Jetson, Qualcomm Ride, Renesas R-Car, Ambarella CV, NXP vision processors, Rockchip, Horizon, Axera, Black Sesame, Nextchip and others
Constraints: Short cable only; custom driver, ISP tuning and EMC design required

Universal architecture: Sensor MIPI → serializer at camera → coax/STP → deserializer → MIPI CSI-2 to SoC.
Compatible compute families: Any SoC with compatible CSI receiver behind a matching TI deserializer/bridge
Advantages: Automotive cable reach, PoC, diagnostics and EMI robustness
Constraints: Not TI-SoC-specific; TI brand applies to SerDes transport only

Universal architecture: Sensor MIPI → Maxim/ADI serializer → coax → deserializer → CSI-2 to SoC.
Compatible compute families: Any SoC with compatible CSI receiver behind the selected ADI deserializer
Constraints: Serializer/deserializer generations and drivers must match

Universal architecture: Camera performs local ISP/compression and streams via 100/1000BASE-T1.
Compatible compute families: Any SoC/domain controller with Ethernet, decoder and time-sync support
Advantages: Long cable, scalable architecture, zonal/domain ECUs
Constraints: Added camera compute, latency, compression and software complexity

Universal architecture: Camera module includes bridge/ISP and presents standard USB video.
Compatible compute families: Windows/Linux boards including AXON, Jetson, x86, RK3588 and many development platforms
Constraints: Usually not deterministic, not automotive, and RAW/exposure control may be restricted

Universal architecture: Sensor uses legacy parallel or vendor LVDS interface; bridge/FPGA may convert to CSI-2.
Compatible compute families: SoCs with native DVP/LVDS or external bridge support
Constraints: Less universal; board routing and driver effort can exceed sensor savings
